compound.name: β-caryophyllene
compound.one_liner: Spicy sesquiterpene (about 10 % of lemon balm oil) that binds the CB2 cannabinoid receptor.

identity.note: PubChem title '(-)-Caryophyllene' (= trans-β-caryophyllene, the natural form).

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Melissa officinalis L., folium. EMA/HMPC/196746/2012 (14 May 2013). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-melissa-officinalis-l-folium_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: EMA: 'β-Caryophyllen and Germacren-D (10% each in the essential oil)'. Duke: BETA-CARYOPHYLLENE Shoot 1-870 ppm. | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil

pharmacology.mechanism: Binds CB2 with functional agonism in human monocytes (adenylate cyclase inhibition, calcium responses); anti-inflammatory in mice only when CB2 is present [40].

evidence.claim: β-caryophyllene is a selective CB2 agonist.
evidence.outcome_summary: Selective CB2 binding with functional agonism.

evidence.claim: β-caryophyllene reduces carrageenan inflammation in mice through CB2.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

compound.teaching_note: A 'dietary cannabinoid' without any psychoactivity: it targets CB2, not the CB1 receptor behind cannabis intoxication [40].
gaps: No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
CB2 Ki not captured (abstract did not state it).
